 NBI busts fake FBI-style scam hub
 Jasper Dawang · 18 November 2026 · 11:23 PM PHT · 2 MIN READ 
 NATIONAL Bureau of Investigation operatives rescue 11 suspected human trafficking victims and arrest three Malaysian nationals during a raid on an alleged online scam hub in Barangay Victoria, Currimao, Ilocos Norte, on 14 November.
 Screengrab from nbi/facebook
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save A makeshift office designed to resemble a United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) facility was among the disturbing discoveries made by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives during a raid on an alleged online scam hub in Barangay Victoria, Currimao, Ilocos Norte, resulting in the rescue of 11 trafficking victims and the arrest of three Malaysian nationals.
 The operation was conducted on 14 November by the NBI-Pampanga District Office (NBI-PAMDO), in coordination with the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office, NBI-Laoag District Office and the Philippine Air Force.
 Investigators discovered that a room on the second floor of the establishment had been converted into a makeshift FBI office, complete with FBI-branded jackets, caps, badges, identification cards, a logo and a United States flag.

 Jasper Dawang · 11 hours ago 
 Authorities believe the items formed part of the setup allegedly used in carrying out fraudulent online activities, although the specific role of the FBI-themed office in the scam operation was not detailed in the initial NBI account.
 The raid stemmed from a complaint involving a woman whose partner was allegedly recruited through an online platform for a supposed virtual assistant position.
 The victim was instructed to report to a workplace along Currimao-Balacad Road in Barangay Victoria on 7 November. However, upon arriving, the individual allegedly discovered that the actual work was entirely different from what had been advertised.
 Instead of performing virtual assistant duties, the employees were allegedly compelled to participate in online scamming activities.
 The victim identified three Malaysian nationals as the individuals allegedly responsible for detaining the employees and forcing them to engage in the illegal operation.
